# From 195 profile items to what can be published

*Figures are generated by `scripts/pilot/accounting.cjs` (output `docs/pilot/accounting.json`) from the profiles as rebuilt after the independent checks. Re-run it after any profile change.*

**These figures are not the ones in the first pilot report.** That report said 194 items, 84 accepted without a person, 85 proposed for a person, 25 unknown, 46 claims and 73 claims. Running independent checks over every item (see `REVIEW_PROCESS.md`) found proposals wider than the sentence quoted for them, including 16 the gate had accepted. They were corrected or sent to a person. The corrected figures are below, and the old ones should be treated as superseded.

| | First report | Now | Why it moved |
|---|---|---|---|
| Profile items | 194 | **195** | One item added: Discover's Saturday club, whose age guide is on a different page from the sentence it was folded into |
| Accepted without a person | 84 | **71** | 13 failed an independent check or a gate rule once their evidence was widened to match what was claimed |
| Proposed for a person | 85 | **99** | The 13, and the new item |
| Unknown or hypothesis | 25 (21 + 4) | **25** (21 + 4) | Unchanged |
| Claims with no person | 46 | **38** | Follows the 71 |
| Claims if every proposal is approved | 73 | **73** | The same facts, approved |

71 + 99 + 25 = 195. One of the 99 is also *held* (Discover's under-1 admission, where two pages disagree); it is never counted as a claim.

## What each number counts

| Number | What it counts | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| **195** | Everything the ten profiles hold: one item per statement a source page makes (or does not make) | profile items |
| **71** | Items that passed the mechanical gate **and** every independent check with no person | profile items |
| **99** | Items held for a person, each with the reason(s) it was held | profile items |
| **25** | Items that are not findings: 21 *unknown* (the pages read do not say) and 4 *hypothesis* ("probably", never shown as fact) | profile items |
| **38** | **Claims** the pilot would write from the 71 without a person | production claim rows |
| **73** | **Claims** it would write if a person approved the 99 as well (the 38 included) | production claim rows |

**38 and 73 are not subsets of 71 and 99.** They are a different unit. An item is not a claim: a claim is one value in one field of the production `venue_claims` table. One item can make two claims (a parking statement that also states a fee makes `parking = yes` and `freeParking = no`), and many items make none, because the table has no field for them.

## Why fewer can be published than were accepted

Where the 71 accepted items go:

| Where it goes | Items | Is the limit a safety gate? |
|---|---|---|
| A claim in a field production already has (toilets, baby changing, café, playground, parking, wheelchair, sensory sessions, accessible parking) | 36 | No. They are publishable. |
| A venue rule or an official-hours reading, two new claim types added in this work | 5 | Needs a person: either can refuse a date or contradict the provider, so it is only ever published from a person-approved claim. |
| **No home at all.** A plain activity description (11), stations/buses/entrances/fees (9), facility detail beyond the mapped fields (4), practical rules (4) | 28 | **No. This is the data model.** The item is accepted and true, and the product has nowhere to put it. |
| A note only | 2 | No. |

Where the 99 held items go if a person approves them:

| Where it goes | Items | Note |
|---|---|---|
| A claim in an existing field | 28 | Becomes 35 claims after parking's second field and the like. |
| A venue rule or an official-hours reading (new) | 27 | Pushchair restrictions, step-free gaps, partial closures, cautions, booking notes, seasonal and conflicting hours. |
| Reviewed activity data (age-specific provision) | 10 | Ships as code through a pull request, not as a claim, by the existing convention. |
| Reviewed admission data | 6 + 7 held | Ships as code; seven are held for a person to decide (a price carried from an earlier reading, an under-1 conflict, four-way day-type prices). |
| No home | 17 | Same data-model limit as above. |
| A note only | 4 | |

## Is this safety, or a pipeline limit?

It is both, and they are separable:

1. **Safety gates (deliberate).** Why the 99 were held, counting the reasons (an item can have several): not a fact type that may be accepted without a person 26; an accessibility claim 21; conditional, temporary or dated wording 17; an independent check doubted it 12; a price or free-entry claim 12; a negative claim 11; says who a place is for 10; conflicts with another reading 9; applies to part of the venue 6; carried from an earlier reading 1. None of these is a defect. Each is a case where an automatic yes would have been wrong at least once in the pilot.
2. **Data-model limits (avoidable).** Before this work 39 accepted items and 19 held ones (plus 22 that survived only as free-text notes) had no field to land in. That is what made the product ignore information it had paid to collect. The two claim types added in this work (venue rules, official hours) give 32 of them a structured home; the tables above are the position after it, with 28 accepted and 17 held items still homeless. What remains without a home is stations and buses, entrance details, and a plain activity description: Venue Detail needs a *transport* field before those can be shown.
3. **Pipeline limits (avoidable).** Production's own automatic publisher only writes 11 field types. Of the 38 claims, **29** are in those 11; the other 9 (picnic area, changing places, accessible parking, and similar) would be published by the pilot's path but not by production's.
4. **Independent check on the extraction.** Running production's own extractor over the same stored pages: it agrees with the profile on 44 facts, disagrees on 2 (two parking statements it would also hold for conflict) and **misses 11** the profile found (toilets, café, and others its patterns do not recognise). So the profile is a superset of what production publishes today, and the 11 are evidence for improving the extractor, not for trusting the profile less.

## So what is "publishable"?

| | Claims | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Written by the pilot with no person | 38 | None, but see 3: production's own publisher would write 29 |
| Written by the pilot if a person approves the held items | 73 | A person approves 35 more claims |
| Venue rules, new in this work | 28 | A person approves each one; nothing automatic can create a rule |
| Official opening hours, new in this work | 16 | A person approves each reading; it can contradict the provider's hours |
| Reviewed activity and admission data | 16 + 7 held | A pull request, by the existing convention |

**Nothing in this branch writes any of these to production.** The fixture builds them locally to show the product.
